topic: Pineapple Shock: This Is What Fresh Pineapple REALLY Does To Your Mouth

beats.narration: Scientists have known for decades that fresh pineapple contains an enzyme that digests protein.
beats.scene: A whole pineapple with a jagged enzyme shape floating above it, molecular dots drifting
beats.label: THE ENZYME

beats.narration: Not a spice. Not an acid. An actual digestive enzyme working on you.
beats.scene: A chili and a lemon both crossed out beside a pineapple, red X marks
beats.label: NOT ACID

beats.narration: Your tongue, your cheeks, the inside of your mouth are made of protein.
beats.scene: A mouth diagram with tongue and cheeks highlighted in bold protein dots
beats.label: YOU ARE PROTEIN

beats.narration: So when you eat pineapple, that enzyme starts breaking down your own tissue.
beats.scene: An enzyme shape snipping tiny links off a pink tongue surface
beats.label: BREAKING YOU DOWN

beats.narration: Stay until the end, because I will show you why that tingle is not acidity.
beats.scene: A tongue with spark marks and a big X over a lemon acid bottle
beats.label: NOT WHAT YOU THINK

beats.narration: And why canned pineapple has been quietly stripped of the one thing that matters.
beats.scene: A sad canned pineapple ring, its glowing core gone, empty middle
beats.label: THE CANNED LIE

beats.narration: This is not about a tropical snack. This is about an enzyme.
beats.scene: A pineapple cocktail with umbrella crossed out, an enzyme shape beside it
beats.label: NOT A SNACK

beats.narration: An enzyme that can digest living tissue, and it is inside your fruit bowl.
beats.scene: A fruit bowl with a pineapple glowing menacingly at the front
beats.label: IN YOUR KITCHEN

beats.narration: Think about the last time you ate fresh pineapple at a summer picnic.
beats.scene: A hand holding a fresh pineapple slice outdoors, picnic blanket behind
beats.label: LAST TIME

beats.narration: Sweet, juicy, cold, and exactly what you wanted on a hot afternoon.
beats.scene: A pineapple slice dripping juice with sun rays and a satisfied face
beats.label: SWEET AND JUICY

beats.narration: Then about a minute in, the edges of your tongue start to feel strange.
beats.scene: A clock at one minute beside an open mouth with question marks
beats.label: ONE MINUTE IN

beats.narration: A tingle. A slight burn. Your tongue feels raw, almost like sandpaper.
beats.scene: A tongue covered in tiny sparks with a rough sandpaper texture patch
beats.label: THE TINGLE

beats.narration: You probably assumed it was the acid in the fruit attacking your mouth.
beats.scene: A lemon squeezing onto a tongue with an arrow labelled acid
beats.label: YOU BLAMED ACID

beats.narration: Maybe you even wondered whether you were secretly mildly allergic to pineapple.
beats.scene: A person scratching their arm with an allergy warning sign above
beats.label: OR AN ALLERGY

beats.narration: But here is what nobody told you at that fruit stand that morning.
beats.scene: A fruit stand with a hidden curtain and a secret glowing behind it
beats.label: NOBODY TOLD YOU

beats.narration: That sensation is not acidity. It is an enzyme called bromelain digesting you.
beats.scene: A bromelain enzyme shape cutting into a tongue with tiny scissors
beats.label: BROMELAIN

beats.narration: Fresh pineapple is not burning your mouth. It is chemically eating you back.
beats.scene: A pineapple with a wide mouth chewing on a tiny running person
beats.label: EATING YOU BACK

beats.narration: Bromelain is not one enzyme. It is a whole family of proteases.
beats.scene: A row of little enzyme characters standing in a family photo line
beats.label: PROTEASES

beats.narration: Proteases cut protein chains apart, exactly like the enzymes in your stomach do.
beats.scene: Scissor-shaped enzymes snipping a long chain of coloured protein beads
beats.label: CUTTING PROTEIN

beats.narration: And in pineapple, this family is concentrated in the stem and the core.
beats.scene: A pineapple cross-section with the tough core glowing bright yellow
beats.label: THE CORE

beats.narration: The fibrous core most people cut away and throw straight into the bin.
beats.scene: A hand dropping a pineapple core into a trash can
beats.label: THROWN AWAY

beats.narration: There is a famous kitchen proof of this, and you have probably seen it.
beats.scene: A kitchen counter with a wobbly bowl of unset jelly and a spoon
beats.label: THE JELL-O PROBLEM

beats.narration: Fresh pineapple in jelly means the jelly never sets, no matter how long you wait.
beats.scene: A bowl of liquid jelly with pineapple chunks, an hourglass beside it
beats.label: IT NEVER SETS

beats.narration: Gelatin is made of collagen, and collagen is a protein. Bromelain eats protein.
beats.scene: A wobbling gelatin cube labelled collagen, an enzyme taking a bite
beats.label: COLLAGEN

beats.narration: So the enzyme chews through the jelly faster than it can ever set.
beats.scene: Enzymes chewing through a jelly cube that keeps collapsing into liquid
beats.label: CHEWED THROUGH

beats.narration: Canned pineapple works perfectly in jelly, and there is one reason only.
beats.scene: A can of pineapple rings beside a perfectly set firm jelly bowl
beats.label: CANNED WORKS

beats.narration: Canning heats the fruit past sixty degrees, and that destroys bromelain permanently.
beats.scene: A pineapple can in a factory with heat waves and a thermometer at sixty
beats.label: HEAT DESTROYS IT

beats.narration: Heat kills the enzyme. That is also why cooked pineapple never tingles.
beats.scene: A grilled pineapple slice with a dead flat enzyme shape beside it
beats.label: HEAT KILLS IT

beats.narration: Roast it, grill it, bake it, and the enzyme is gone before it reaches your plate.
beats.scene: Pineapple on a grill with the enzyme vanishing upward in steam
beats.label: GONE

beats.narration: Here is where the story genuinely turns. The enzyme does not stop at your mouth.
beats.scene: An enzyme walking past a mouth signpost heading down a tunnel
beats.label: IT GOES DEEPER

beats.narration: Bromelain is one of the very few food enzymes that survives your stomach acid.
beats.scene: An enzyme swimming through a bubbling acid pool, unharmed and smiling
beats.label: SURVIVES THE STOMACH

beats.narration: It reaches your small intestine intact, and from there it enters your bloodstream.
beats.scene: An enzyme passing through an intestine wall into a red bloodstream river
beats.label: INTO THE BLOOD

beats.narration: Once it is circulating in your body, it does three measurable things.
beats.scene: A clipboard with three numbered boxes, the enzyme standing beside it
beats.label: THREE THINGS

beats.narration: It breaks down fibrin, the protein mesh that forms around injured tissue.
beats.scene: A net of fibrin around a wound being snipped apart by enzymes
beats.label: FIBRIN

beats.narration: It suppresses the signalling molecules that drive pain and swelling after injury.
beats.scene: Pain signal molecules blocked by stop signs held up by enzymes
beats.label: PAIN SIGNALS

beats.narration: And it thins mucus, which is why it shows up in sinus treatments.
beats.scene: Thick gloopy mucus turning thin and watery with a happy sinus diagram
beats.label: THINS MUCUS

beats.narration: German surgeons have given bromelain to patients after operations to reduce swelling.
beats.scene: A surgeon in scrubs handing a bromelain capsule to a bandaged patient
beats.label: GERMAN SURGEONS

beats.narration: It is a recognised treatment for sinus inflammation across several European countries.
beats.scene: A map of Europe with a calm sinus diagram glowing over it
beats.label: SINUS TREATMENT

beats.narration: Clinical trials have measured it reducing joint pain in people with osteoarthritis.
beats.scene: A knee joint diagram with pain stars fading away one by one
beats.label: JOINT PAIN

beats.narration: Not in a petri dish. Not in mice. In actual human beings.
beats.scene: A petri dish and a mouse both crossed out, a human figure highlighted
beats.label: IN HUMANS

beats.narration: But the part that shocked even the researchers is how selective this enzyme is.
beats.scene: A researcher with wide eyes, clipboard shaking, magnifying glass on enzyme
beats.label: SHOCKED RESEARCHERS

beats.narration: Most anti-inflammatory drugs blunt your entire immune system, like a heavy hammer.
beats.scene: A giant hammer squashing a whole army of immune cells flat
beats.label: BLUNT TOOL

beats.narration: Bromelain does something smarter. It works like a scalpel instead of a hammer.
beats.scene: An enzyme holding a fine laser scalpel, precision glowing at the tip
beats.label: SMARTER

beats.narration: It selectively reduces the signalling molecules that cause swelling, and nothing else.
beats.scene: Only the red swelling signal being snipped while green signals float past
beats.label: SELECTIVE

beats.narration: The rest of your immune response keeps working exactly as it should.
beats.scene: Healthy immune cells standing in formation, untouched and saluting
beats.label: LEFT ALONE

beats.narration: No approved drug works through this pathway, at this dose, from this food.
beats.scene: A medicine bottle shrugging beside a fresh pineapple with a trophy
beats.label: NO DRUG DOES THIS

beats.narration: So what do you actually do with this? Three steps. Simple. Specific.
beats.scene: A bold title card with three steps written in hand-drawn capitals
beats.label: THREE STEPS

beats.narration: Step one: eat fresh pineapple, never canned, because canning destroys the enzyme.
beats.scene: A fresh pineapple with a tick beside a can with a cross
beats.label: STEP ONE: FRESH

beats.narration: Step two: never cook it. Heat above sixty degrees kills bromelain permanently.
beats.scene: A thermometer at sixty degrees with a flame and a dead enzyme
beats.label: STEP TWO: NEVER COOK

beats.narration: Step three: eat the core, because that is where the protease concentration is highest.
beats.scene: A pineapple core glowing with a concentration bar chart at maximum
beats.label: STEP THREE: EAT THE CORE

beats.narration: This is all in the scientific literature, but almost nobody communicates it properly.
beats.scene: A tall stack of research papers with a tiny megaphone beside them
beats.label: NOBODY SAYS IT

beats.narration: That gap between the research and your kitchen is exactly what Food Code exists to close.
beats.scene: A bridge being built between a laboratory and a home kitchen counter
beats.label: THE MISSION

beats.narration: After today, you are no longer someone who eats pineapple without thinking twice.
beats.scene: A person transformed, glowing brain, looking thoughtfully at a pineapple
beats.label: YOU CHANGED

beats.narration: You understand what bromelain does to protein, and why your tongue tingles.
beats.scene: A brain with a bromelain label connecting dots to a tingling tongue
beats.label: YOU UNDERSTAND

beats.narration: You know why the canned stuff is dead, and why heat destroys everything.
beats.scene: A dead flat enzyme in a can beside a flame, both labelled dead
beats.label: YOU KNOW WHY

beats.narration: That knowledge changes every single decision you make in the produce aisle.
beats.scene: A supermarket produce aisle with a glowing arrow to the fresh pineapples
beats.label: EVERY DECISION

beats.narration: Tell me in the comments, have you ever felt that tingle on your tongue?
beats.scene: A speech bubble comment box with a tingling tongue emoji inside
beats.label: TELL ME

beats.narration: I read every single one of them, and I answer the good ones.
beats.scene: A stack of comment cards, one with a reply badge, a pen ready
beats.label: I READ THEM

beats.narration: In the next video, I am going to show you what ginger does to your stomach.
beats.scene: A ginger root with a spotlight, a stomach diagram waiting beside it
beats.label: NEXT: GINGER

beats.narration: Not your immune system, not your cells, your stomach. And it is not nothing.
beats.scene: Immune system and cells crossed out, stomach circled with a warning star
beats.label: YOUR STOMACH
